assumptions: The structured `cycle` field on check-deps circularDeps stays ABSOLUTE (unchanged contract); only the human/JSON `message` becomes repo-relative, carried on a new `message` field like layerViolations already has.
Correcting the cycle array changes the arch `circular-deps` violation id (it hashes the chain) for any existing cycle once; this repo's baseline has zero circular-deps ids so nothing here moves.

Out of scope: for an SCC with branching edges, Tarjan discovery order is not always a real import walk (consecutive pairs may lack an edge). Linear 2- and 3-file cycles, the reported case, are real walks.
rootCause: detectCircularDeps (packages/core/src/constraints/circular-deps.ts) closed each cycle with `reversed[reversed.length - 1]` - the LAST node - instead of `reversed[0]`, so the data array itself was `[b, a, a]` (a fake self-edge). check-deps then joined the absolute paths verbatim into the message while `file` was already posix-relative.

reproduction.after: core chain test 3 passed (3); cli chain test 2 passed (2)
